headline: UPDATE TO totw-20261108-0700-02 (two tankers) -- IN-WINDOW
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM as stated; the EVENT Unverified] The IRGC Navy says three non-compliant oil tankers exploded and caught fire while sailing an 'illegal channel' in the Strait of Hormuz since the early hours of Sunday Nov 8, after switching off their navigation and identification systems;…
sources: IRGC Navy statement, via Press TV (IRNA/Sepah News origin)
fault_line: Are tankers really hitting Iranian mines in a strait CENTCOM says it cleared -- or is Tehran claiming fires it did not cause to enforce its blockade by fear? And who pays: the shippers, or drivers at the pump?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM as stated; the EVENT Unverified] The IRGC Navy says three non-compliant oil tankers exploded and caught fire while sailing an 'illegal channel' in the Strait of Hormuz since the early hours of Sunday Nov 8, after switching off their navigation and identification systems; thick smoke from the burning vessels is spreading across the strait. WION frames it as 'a third oil tanker' -- i.e. the count rose 2 -> 3 from the Saturday-late statement (two tankers, recorded 0700-02). No vessel names or nationalities given. AFP (via FMT/Gulf News) notes it was unable to confirm whether the various reports (IRGC claim, UKMTO Khasab fire, UAE 22-crew rescue) reference the same incidents.
sections.what_verified: 2 tiered families for the statement: IRGC/Press TV (T3, STATE IR -- the actor's own statement) + AFP (T1) relaying the statement via FMT and Gulf News. Gulf News (T3) carries the AFP relay, so it counts as the AFP family, not a second family. WION, Seatrade and stockmarketwatch are unregistered and add no corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: CENTCOM said last month it helped Gulf countries export 1.5bn barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said all mines have been cleared from the waterway. UKMTO has confirmed no mine strike; its only Nov 8 advisory (199-26) is a delayed report of a tanker fire off Khasab with cause unknown. No vessel has been named in any IRGC mine claim since Oct 29 (Mehr archive: similar 2- and 3-tanker claims on Oct 29, Oct 31, Nov 2, Nov 3, Nov 5, Nov 6).
sections.why_matters: Two tankers yesterday, three today -- Iran says its mines are still biting in Hormuz while America says the strait is cleared. The count keeps rising; the proof never arrives.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE TO totw-20261108-0700-02 (two tankers) -- IN-WINDOW (Press TV 11:04 GMT = 15:04 ; Gulf News standalone 15:23 ; WION 16:59 IST = 15:29 ; FMT/AFP 19:34 MYT = 15:34 ) -- IRGC Navy now says THREE oil tankers exploded and caught fire in Hormuz since the early hours of Sunday

totw_analysis: Our read: Two tankers yesterday, three today -- Iran says its mines are still biting in Hormuz while America says the strait is cleared. The count keeps rising; the proof never arrives. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Are tankers really hitting Iranian mines in a strait CENTCOM says it cleared -- or is Tehran claiming fires it did not cause to enforce its blockade by fear? And who pays: the shippers, or drivers at the pump?
